Carlos — quick technical answers and proposal from our infra side:

1) Session churn and short-lived sessions
- Dedicated pool handles churn by maintaining hot lanes (worker threads) and KV partitioning per tenant. Short-lived spikes primarily increase scheduling overhead; to mitigate we recommend a small connection fronting layer (nginx/edge-proxy) with connection pooling enabled so sessions reuse established connections. That reduces p99 noise.

2) Long-output bursts (2k tokens)
- Large outputs increase per-session token emission time but much of the cost shifts to per-token compute. For long bursts we suggest: (a) increase per-host token batching limit, (b) enable adaptive micro-batching (we can push a config change for the canary), and (c) pre-allocate larger KV cache footprints for the specific user cohorts that produce long outputs. With those, our bench suggests p95 stays within target; p99 will depend on network tail but should stabilize <700ms for token emits in most runs.

3) Cold KV warm-up
- Warm-up time depends on cache size and retrieval pattern; empirically we see 10–60s to reach steady-state for small-to-medium caches (per-shard). For predictable behavior we recommend a 10–30 minute pre-warm step during the canary by replaying a small sample of hot sessions (we can run the replay). We also provide an automated warmup script that touches hot prefixes.

Proposed canary config (technical):
- Pool size: 8 GPU hosts (A100-equivalent) dedicated to EdgeStream pilot
- Adaptive micro-batching: enabled; batching window target 10–25ms
- KV pre-warm: 15m pre-run using your sample traces
- Observability: token-level tracing + per-session emit timestamps retained for 90 days (audit log location: S3 path, will provide IAM role)
- Rollout: start at 30% traffic (50 concurrent), increase to 100% over 90 minutes while monitoring p95/p99 and error budget consumption

MAP items I can own: setup of replay harness, push micro-batching config, and provide a roll-forward plan for quantized model fallback. Jasmine — if EdgeStream confirms concurrency numbers we’ll scope the pool.
